h: Joseph and the Hope of Final Redemption

p: וַיִּשְׁתּוּ וַיִּשְׁכְּרוּ עִמּוֹ.
— “They drank and became intoxicated with him.”

הִנֵּה מַה שֶּׁשָּׁתוּ יֵשׁ לוֹמַר מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָיָה אָז סְעוּדַת שַׁבָּת, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה: אֵין הָכֵן אֶלָּא שַׁבָּת, וּבְשַׁבָּתוֹת אָדָם קוֹבֵעַ סְעוּדָתוֹ עַל הַיַּיִן (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרָכוֹת מב:).

— One can explain their drinking as due to its being a Shabbat meal, as Bereishis Rabbah states: “‘Prepare’ refers specifically to Shabbat.” On Shabbat, a person establishes his meal with wine (as stated in Berachos 42b).
אֲבָל לְהִשְׁתַּכֵּר לֹא מָצִינוּ.
— Yet we do not find an obligation to become intoxicated.
וְאִיתָא (סַנְהֶדְרִין ע:): וּלְרוֹזְנִים אֵי שֵׁכָר, מִי שֶׁכָּל רָזֵי עוֹלָם גְּלוּיִם לוֹ יִשְׁתֶּה יַיִן וְיִשְׁתַּכֵּר?
— It is taught (Sanhedrin 70b): “‘Nor for rulers, intoxicating drink’—should one to whom all the world's mysteries are revealed drink wine and become intoxicated?”
וּבְשַׁבָּת יִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹסְקִין בְּרָזֵי עוֹלָם, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: יְגַלֵּה לָן טַעֲמֵי וְכוּלֵי, חֲדוּ חָצְדֵי חַקְלָא וְכוּלֵי, וּבְוַדַּאי אֵינוֹ זְמַן שִׁכְרוּת.
— On Shabbat, Israel engage in the world's mysteries, as we say: “May He reveal to us the reasons,” etc., “Rejoice, reapers of the field,” etc. Surely this is no time for intoxication.
וְהִנֵּה הַשְּׁבָטִים יֵשׁ לוֹמַר שֶׁשָּׁתוּ מֵהֶכְרֵחַ לְקַיֵּים גְּזֵירַת מוֹשֵׁל מִצְרַיִם, וְאִם נִשְׁתַּכְּרוּ אַחַר כָּךְ מַה הֲוָה לְהוּ לְמֶיעְבַּד.
— Regarding the tribes, one can say that they drank under compulsion, to comply with the Egyptian ruler's decree. If they subsequently became intoxicated, what could they have done?
אֲבָל יוֹסֵף יֵשׁ לְהָבִין לָמָּה שָׁתָה לְשָׁכְרָה.
— But why Joseph drank to intoxication requires explanation.

h: Purim and the Eradication of Amalek

p: אָמְנָם בְּפוּרִים מָצִינוּ (מְגִילָּה ז:): מִיחַיֵּיב אִינִשׁ לְבַסּוּמֵי בְּפוּרַיָּא עַד דְּלָא יָדַע וְכוּלֵי.
— On Purim, however, we find (Megillah 7b): “A person is obligated to become intoxicated on Purim until he does not know,” etc.
וְהַיְינוּ דַּעֲמָלֵק שׁוֹרֶשׁ כָּל הַקְּלִיפּוֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם עֲמָלֵק.
— For Amalek is the root of all the kelipos, as it says: “Amalek is the first of the nations.”
וּכְשֶׁיִּהְיֶה גְּמַר מְחִיַּית עֲמָלֵק, בֶּאֱמֶת בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא יִהְיֶה הַשֵּׁם אֶחָד וְגוֹמֵר, שֶׁיִּתְבַּטְּלוּ כָּל הַקְּלִיפּוֹת.
— When Amalek's eradication is complete, truly “On that day Hashem will be One,” etc., for all the kelipos will be nullified.
וּבְפוּרִים, הַזְּמַן הַמְיוּחָד שֶׁהָיָה בוֹ מְחִיַּית עֲמָלֵק, רֵאשִׁית דִּקְלִיפָּה,
— Purim is the appointed time in which Amalek, the first of the kelipah, was eradicated.

וְעַל כֵּן יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִצְוַת שִׁכְרוּת, שֶׁמּוֹרָה שֶׁאַף שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעַת הַיִּשְׂרָאֵל קָשׁוּר בְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ רֵאשִׁית דִּקְדוּשָׁה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: בְּרֵאשִׁית, בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ רֵאשִׁית.

— It therefore includes a mitzvah of intoxication, indicating that even without conscious awareness, a Jew is bound to the root of the first principle of holiness. As it is said: “Bereishis”—for the sake of Israel, who are called “first.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Resisei Layla §20: “This holiness is revealed in its full strength on Purim, when they said, ‘One must become intoxicated until he does not know.’ Its plain meaning is the revelation that the hearts of Israel are truly attached to God even when they cannot distinguish their right from their left. A person is recognized through three things, including his cup and his intoxication, for then he lacks the full awareness needed to conceal and cover the depths of his heart. What lies within those depths is then revealed, as they said, ‘Wine enters, the secret emerges.’ It becomes revealed that the depths of Israel’s heart are attached to God without any deliberate reflection or coercion of the heart’s will. Rather, the true point of desire is truly attached to God of itself.”

p: וְכֵן יוֹסֵף הָיָה סָבוּר שֶׁהוּא מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף, וּכְבָר נִתְבָּרְרוּ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל וְעַל יָדוֹ יִהְיֶה מְחִיַּית עֲמָלֵק שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַקְּלִיפּוֹת.
— Likewise, Joseph thought that he was Mashiach ben Joseph, that all Israel had already been refined, and that Amalek, the root of the kelipos, would be eradicated through him.
וּכְבָר פָּעַל יוֹסֵף בְּמִצְרַיִם גַּם כֵּן שֶׁפַּרְעֹה הִכִּיר בְּשֵׁם אֱלֹהִים, שֶׁאָמַר: אַחֲרֵי הוֹדִיעַ אֱלֹהִים וְגוֹמֵר, וְשֵׁם זֶה קוֹדֶשׁ.
— Joseph had already brought about recognition of the Name Elokim even in Egypt. Pharaoh said: “Since God has made known,” etc.; this occurrence of the Name is sacred.
שֶׁזֶּה פָּעַל יוֹסֵף, שֶׁהִכְנִיס אַף בְּפַרְעֹה שֶׁיַּאֲמִין בֵּאלֹהִים.
— Joseph accomplished this: he instilled belief in God even in Pharaoh.
וְגַם פַּרְעֹה הִסְכִּים עַל הַמִּילָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ, וְהָיָה סָבוּר שֶׁכְּבָר בָּא הַזְּמַן שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַתִּיקּוּן.
— Pharaoh also consented to circumcision, as stated in the Midrash. Joseph thought that the time for the repair had already arrived.

וְאָז הָיָה שַׁבָּת, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת מִיָּד נִגְאָלִין, וְרָצָה לְהַכְנִיס קְדוּשַׁת הַשַּׁבָּת בְּאֶחָיו גַּם כֵּן, וְיִהְיֶה מְחִיַּית עֲמָלֵק רֵאשִׁית דִּקְלִיפָּה, וְזֶהוּ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וַיִּשְׁכְּרוּ עִמּוֹ.

— It was Shabbat, whose observance brings immediate redemption. He wished to impart Shabbat holiness to his brothers as well, bringing about the eradication of Amalek, the first of the kelipah. This is the meaning of “They became intoxicated with him.”

וּבָזֶה יוּבַן מַה שֶּׁיִּפָּלֵא לִכְאוֹרָה עַל יוֹסֵף, שֶׁאַחַר שֶׁאָכַל וְשָׁתָה עִמָּהֶם, לָמָּה זֶּה צִיעֵר אוֹתָם אַחַר כָּךְ בְּמַעֲשֵׂה הַגָּבִיעַ, וְהָיָה לוֹ לְהִתְגַּלּוֹת לִפְנֵיהֶם וְלִשְׁלוֹחַ וּלְהָבִיא אֶת יַעֲקֹב.

— This explains what otherwise seems puzzling about Joseph: after eating and drinking with them, why did he then distress them through the affair of the goblet? He should have revealed himself to them and sent to bring Jacob.

אַךְ לְפִי הָאָמוּר, מִתְּחִלָּה הָיָה סָבוּר שֶׁכְּבָר עָשָׂה מְחִיַּית עֲמָלֵק, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהוּא נִתְבָּרֵר בִּשְׁלֵימוּת בְּמִדָּתוֹ, כֵּן גַּם כָּל הַשְּׁבָטִים נִתְבָּרְרוּ וְעָשׂוּ תְשׁוּבָה כְּשֶׁאָמְרוּ: אֲבָל אֲשֵׁמִים אֲנַחְנוּ וְגוֹמֵר.

— According to the above, at first he thought that he had already eradicated Amalek. Just as he had been completely refined in his own attribute, so too all the tribes had been refined and repented when they said: “Indeed, we are guilty,” etc.
וְהָיָה סָבוּר שֶׁעַל יְדֵי שַׁבָּת יִהְיוּ נִגְאָלִין מִיָּד וְיִהְיֶה הוּא כְּמוֹ מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף.
— He thought that through Shabbat they would be redeemed immediately and he would be like Mashiach ben Joseph.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Lech Lecha 4:1: “Likewise, ‘They drank and became intoxicated with him’ took place at a Shabbat meal, as it says (Bereishis Rabbah 92), ‘“Prepare” refers only to Shabbat.’ On Shabbat the will of Atika is revealed: by day, the meal of Atika, and at the third meal Zeir Anpin and Atika come to dine with her. Daas, the inwardness of Keser, is revealed, and therefore drinking is permitted on it. This is why Joseph’s brothers drank then, even though they had not drunk for all twenty-two years: Joseph shone the holiness of Shabbat upon them, they sensed the holiness of the Shabbat meal, and they drank. Joseph’s intention in giving them drink was that he wished to know the depths of their hearts, whether they are bound to the root, as in Sanhedrin, ‘When wine enters, a secret comes out.’ As for intoxication, as we find, ‘A person is obligated to become intoxicated on Purim,’ even though in holiness we find only the drinking of wine … that applies at the eradication of Amalek, the first of the kelipah. Then Israel are shown to be bound to the first thought, … and once this is made clear there is intoxication in holiness as well. So too the tribes then sensed the holiness at the Shabbat meal Joseph made for them.”

He adds that Joseph gave them wine to learn whether their hearts were bound to the root, which matches Joseph’s belief here that the tribes had already been refined.

h: Further Repentance Before the Appointed Time

p: אֲבָל אַחַר כָּךְ רָאָה שֶׁהַקְּלִיפָּה בִּתְקִיפוּתָהּ, וְהֵבִין מִזֶּה שֶׁעֲדַיִין לֹא נִתְבָּרְרוּ כָּל הַשְּׁבָטִים,
— Afterward, however, he saw that the kelipah remained powerful, and understood from this that not all the tribes had yet been refined.
וְעָשָׂה תַּחְבּוּלָה כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּצְטַעֲרוּ וְיָשׁוּבוּ בִּתְשׁוּבָה שְׁלֵמָה, וְאַחַר כָּךְ יִתְוַדַּע אֶל אֶחָיו.
— He therefore devised a plan so that they would suffer distress and return in complete repentance, after which he would reveal himself to his brothers.

רַק אַחַר כָּךְ וְלֹא יָכוֹל יוֹסֵף לְהִתְאַפֵּק וְגוֹמֵר, וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁמִּצִּדּוֹ רָצָה לְהִתְאַפֵּק עוֹד עַד שֶׁיָּשׁוּבוּ בֶּאֱמֶת וִיתַקְּנוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַקִּלְקוּל, וְיִהְיֶה גְּמַר הַתִּיקּוּן עַל יָדוֹ, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף,

— Yet afterward, “Joseph could not restrain himself,” etc. For his part, he wished to hold back longer, until they truly repented and repaired the root of the corruption, so that the final repair would come through him as Mashiach ben Joseph.
אַךְ לֹא יָכוֹל לְהִתְאַפֵּק וְגוֹמֵר.
— But “he could not restrain himself,” etc.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב רַבִּי מֹשֶׁה בֶּן נַחְמָן: כִּי אֲנָשִׁים רַבִּים חִילּוּ פָנָיו שֶׁיִּמְחוֹל לְבִנְיָמִין, כִּי נִכְמְרוּ רַחֲמֵיהֶם עַל תַּחֲנוּנֵי יְהוּדָה וְכוּלֵי.
— As Ramban writes: “Many people implored him to forgive Benjamin, for their compassion was stirred by Judah's pleas,” etc.
וְזֶה הָיָה מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם, כֵּיוָן שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה עוֹד זְמַן מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף.
— This was from Heaven, since the time of Mashiach ben Joseph had not yet arrived.

וְלָכֵן נָתַן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּלִבָּם שֶׁיְחַלּוּ פָנָיו, וְלֹא יָכוֹל לְהִתְאַפֵּק וְנִתְוַדַּע עֲלֵיהֶם, אַף שֶׁעֲדַיִין לֹא תִקְּנוּ הַכֹּל מִצִּדָּם שֶׁיִּזְכּוּ לִהְיוֹת גְּמַר הַתִּיקּוּן, עַד עֵת בּוֹא דְבָרוֹ וְיָבֹא מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף מִזַּרְעוֹ.

— Hashem therefore moved them to implore him. He could no longer restrain himself and revealed himself to them, although they had not yet repaired everything on their part so as to merit the final repair. This awaits the appointed fulfillment of His word, when Mashiach ben Joseph will come from his descendants.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Shmuel Bornsztain of Sochatchov, Shem MiShmuel, Vayigash 9:11: “The whole reason Joseph had not informed his father until now was that he wished everything to be done by the Blessed One Himself, who would make it known, and not through human arousal and human grasping. … The tribes, although righteous, with the holy spirit resting upon them, were all occupied with their sackcloth and fasting, as in the Midrash, and so the Shekhinah did not rest upon them. He deliberated whether the time had come for it to be made known to them from Heaven, but this was impossible because they were steeped in sadness. Therefore he made the meal before them. The Midrash says, ‘“Prepare” refers only to Shabbat,’ so it was a Shabbat meal, all the more so a meal at the table of Joseph, who was himself the aspect of Shabbat, to lift their hearts so that they would forget their sadness of spirit. And so it was, until ‘they drank and became intoxicated with him.’ … In this way they became fit for the holy spirit, and he thought that once the holy spirit returned to them, perhaps it would be a time of favor for it to be made known from Heaven. But when he saw that this too did not help, he thought that they still lacked cleansing for the sin of the sale. Therefore he devised the scheme of the goblet, until they accepted upon themselves to be slaves, all of them, a repentance in equal measure for having sold him as a slave. … Joseph himself did not want to reveal himself, and so he wished to restrain himself further, until the word of Hashem came from Heaven to tell him what to do.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: The Shem MiShmuel follows the same sequence as Rav Tzadok: a Shabbat meal meant to bring the redemptive moment, and then, when it did not come, the goblet as further cleansing for the sale. He adds that the goblet brought them to a measure-for-measure teshuvah, accepting slavery for selling Joseph as a slave, and that Joseph’s restraint came from his wish that the revelation come from Heaven alone.

paragraphs.text: Ramban on Genesis 45:1: “The correct explanation in my view is that many members of Pharaoh’s household and other Egyptians were present and implored him to forgive Benjamin, because their compassion had been stirred by Judah’s pleas. Joseph could not hold firm against them all, and he called to his servants, “Remove every outsider from me, for I will speak with them.” They went out, and as they left he raised his voice in weeping. The Egyptians and the members of Pharaoh’s household who had just gone out heard him, for they were still in the outer courtyard.”
